text:
Morgan Li: Heads up — I'm going to temporarily raise the prod `api` error-rate alert from 2% -> 5% for 30m while we triage a noisy Redis/alb spike. Suppressing paging for noisy flapping. Will document actions below.

IncidentBot: Alert config change recorded by Morgan Li. alert_id: ALRT-9021, old_threshold=2%, new_threshold=5%, suppression=30m. Audit: <https://console.redwood/internal/alerts/ALRT-9021> :information_source:

Sasha R: quick q — who's primary on this shift? any coverage gaps we should be aware of?

Morgan Li: I'm primary for the window 13:00-15:00 PT. TJ is secondary. Oncall handoff scheduled at 14:50 PT; TJ is overlapping until 15:20 PT. There's a 00:40 gap overnight later (02:00–02:40 UTC) that we already flagged to rotations team. For this incident we'll handle live. :white_check_mark:

TJ: I'm available as secondary. If the threshold change doesn't stop noisy pages I can take an active look at replica failovers and connection pooling.

Oncall Ops: Attaching runbook pointer and quick rollback steps. Runbook: <https://runbooks.redwood/triage/error-rate-flap>. Revert command (console):

```bash
# revert alert threshold to previous value
redwoodctl alerts update ALRT-9021 --threshold 2
# cancel suppression if you want immediate paging back on
redwoodctl alerts cancel-suppression ALRT-9021
```

Eva Chen: Customer impact summary from monitoring: between 12:58-13:12 UTC we saw short bursts of 502/504s concentrated on eu-west-1 and us-west-2. About 4 paying customers reported degraded experiences (support tickets #4532, #4539). We engaged the fallback cluster routing at 13:05 which brought error rates down. Estimated user-facing error spike ~0.03% of total requests.

Zach P: Quick note on SLOs — current SLO is 99.9% success over 30d. If the spike continues unchanged we project a 0.02 percentage point hit to the 30d window (still within buffer), but we want to avoid alert fatigue. Hence the temporary threshold bump while we patch root cause.

Sasha R: Ok good to know. What's the mitigation plan for Redis noise?

Morgan Li: Steps executed / in progress: 
- Scaled read replica pool in eu-west-1 (+2 nodes) at 13:06.
- Enabled connection backpressure between API pool and Redis at 13:07 (circuit breaker param lowered).
- Rolling restart of the problem proxy slice scheduled at 13:20 (done).
- Investigating noisy autoscaler flapping that correlates with a periodic batch job.

TJ: If the autoscaler is the culprit we should consider adding a short stabilization window (5m) and increase the min replicas for the proxy group. I'll open the change in infra and tag @infra-approvals.

Oncall Ops: Noted. I created infra change CHG-1187 to add stabilization=300s for proxy-autoscaler minimum during peak hours. We can roll out as emergency config if noise recurs.

IncidentBot: Paging suppressed for ALRT-9021 until 13:43 UTC per manual action by Morgan Li. Suppression reason: retriable infra noise, manual triage in progress.

Eva Chen: Customer comms plan: support will triage top 4 affected accounts; if we see repeated SLA violations we'll issue pro-rata credits as per SLA. For now we have no confirmed SLA breach.

Sasha R: Anything for the post-incident notes / threshold tuning? We should capture lessons (when to raise vs. when to tune alert definitions).

Morgan Li: Agreed. Action items to add to post-incident doc: 
- Add a time-windowed mute option to alerting (mute short spikes without full suppression).
- Re-evaluate ALRT-9021 sensitivity — consider CPU / latency correlation to avoid Redis-flap noise.
- Follow-up with infra to add stabilization to proxy autoscaler (CHG-1187).
- Create a quick checklist for on-call handoff: primary/secondary visibility, planned suppressions, runbook links.

TJ: I'll own the autoscaler change and come back with an ETA.

Oncall Ops: Logging the suppression action and transcription in the incident tracker now: INC-2026-33. Please add any slack notes you want preserved.

Morgan Li: I'll post a short summary to the incident channel once the metrics look stable. For now plan: keep suppression 30m, continue mitigations, no escalation to SRE lead unless error-rate > 6% or customer reports increase. If anything changes ping @Sasha R and @TJ directly.

Sasha R: Acknowledged. Thanks for handling the noisy pages and leaving clear runbook + revert steps. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Thread archived at 13:48 UTC. Reminder: please fill the postmortem template within 72h: <https://incidents.redwood/templates/slo-threshold-change>
